seoTitle: Instagram Ad Account Disabled: Reasons & Recovery Guide
metaDescription: Understand why your Instagram ad account got disabled and how to check your account status and submit an appeal to recover it.
intro: A disabled Instagram ad account can stop your campaigns cold, and figuring out why is the first step toward getting it back. This guide covers the common causes, how to check your account status, and how to submit an appeal through Facebook's tools since Instagram ads run through Ads Manager.

steps.heading: Understand why it was disabled
steps.body: Common causes include violating advertising policies, suspicious activity like creating too many ads quickly, or billing issues such as an expired card or unpaid balance.

steps.heading: Check your account status
steps.body: Open Instagram, go to your Profile, tap the menu icon, go to Settings and Privacy, then Account and Account Status to see whether ads or content have been flagged.

steps.heading: Submit an appeal
steps.body: Go to the Facebook Business Help Center or the Facebook Account Quality page, submit a request for review, and fill out the appeal form explaining why you believe the account was disabled in error.

steps.heading: Wait for a response
steps.body: After submitting the appeal, Facebook or Instagram will review it and respond by email, so keep an eye on your inbox.

faq.question: Why was my Instagram ad account disabled?
faq.answer: Common reasons include violating advertising policies, unusual account activity, or billing problems like an expired card or unpaid balance.

faq.question: How do I check why my account was flagged?
faq.answer: Go to Settings and Privacy, then Account, then Account Status to see details on any flagged ads or content.

faq.question: How do I appeal a disabled ad account?
faq.answer: Submit a review request through the Facebook Business Help Center or the Facebook Account Quality page, explaining why you believe it was disabled by mistake.

faq.question: How long does an appeal take?
faq.answer: The response time varies, but Facebook or Instagram will notify you by email once your appeal has been reviewed.
